serie: Sachiko's Home: an 80-year-old Japanese grandmother from Osaka, in America since 1970, shares the Japanese ways to keep a house clean, light and calm: order, cleaning, fresh air, and what to throw out
acciones: folding a cloth, putting things in a wooden box, airing a futon over a rail, spraying a brown bottle on tile grout, wiping a shelf, writing on the back of a photograph
estilo: One ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by her grandson with a phone at eye level, in the middle of the action: framing casual and a little off, something cut by the edge of the frame, almost everything in focus and nothing blurred out, only the light the place really has (a ceiling bulb, a lamp or the daylight from the window), automatic white balance a bit off, slight phone noise, ordinary worn objects of an old Iowa farmhouse, plain bottles and rags with no labels, no beautiful composition.

sachiko.desc: Sachiko Okada, a 78-year-old Japanese grandmother with short permed grey hair, a mustard yellow knit cardigan over a white blouse and a red gingham apron

lugares_fijos.casa: Sachiko's small old American house arranged the Japanese way: tatami mat in the living room, a low wooden shelf, a shoji screen, a genkan entry step with slippers, soft grey window light

identidad: Preserve the exact identity, face, short permed grey hair, age and skin of the elderly Japanese woman in the reference photograph. She wears a mustard yellow knit cardigan over a white blouse and a red gingham apron.
